objective.subject: fix: address the first adversarial review of the join-policy change
objective.body:
Review run join-policy-await-all-ce7b5cc2-20261128-125101-c0b616 (codex on
zcode/GLM-5.4) reported six findings; run ...-125057-d99db7 (codex on
deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro) reported none. All six reproduced against the
working tree and are fixed here:

- codex:1 (defect): under AWAIT_ALL, mapAndCombine gated its combine through
  Futures.allAsList(views), so every element failure after the first was
  logged at SEVERE as "Got more than one input Future failure". The AWAIT_ALL
  gate is now one successfulAsList listener that submits the combine when all
  elements succeeded and skips it otherwise. The new
  severalElementFailuresUnderAwaitAllAreNotLoggedAsAggregateFailures fails
  without the fix ([SEVERE, SEVERE]); the test class no longer mutes the
  aggregate logger.
- codex:5 (test quality): the two deadline-after-failure tests used a real
  200 ms deadline that a loaded runner could hit before the failure settled;
  they now advance a ManualClock after the outcomes are recorded.
  ScopeTerminationOrderTest's caller-parked wait now fails instead of
  silently giving up.
- codex:0 (contract text): JoinPolicy and cancellation-propagation.md 1.1
  said a direct member cancellation leaves siblings ABORTED_BY_FAIL_FAST; in a
  group it cancels the group token and siblings read
  CANCELLED_BY_PARENT_SCOPE, unchanged behavior that the text now states.
- codex:2 (public docs): JoinPolicy, GroupStart, the user guides, the
  graveyard and philosophy pages, and the changelog listed close() among the
  cancellation sources; the scope close() is package-private and
  ParRuntime.close() does not cancel admitted work, so it is removed there.
- codex:3, codex:4 (contract drift): task-group-cancellation.md still
  described the single-CAS, cancellation-first scope derivation, and
  task-group-lifecycle.md and the adopt Javadoc stated the fail-fast cascade
  without the policy qualification.

MUST: under AWAIT_ALL, no aggregate over a batch's element futures logs an
ordinary element failure.
